summary: MoMo payer-vs-merchant safety-guard verification. 12/14 backend tests PASS. Frontend: all 8 review-request UI assertions PASS. CRITICAL SAFETY BUG DISCOVERED: `_normalize_msisdn` in server.py:728-733 does NOT convert the 10-digit local Rwandan format `0798875272` to `250798875272`. Result: when a user types the merchant number as `0798875272`, the guard `_guard_payer_not_merchant` fails to match (compares '0798875272' vs '250798875272') and the request reaches BeSoft. Same bug affects both /api/billing/momo/initiate and /api/billing/vod/{id}/momo endpoints. All other formats (`+250798875272`, `250798875272`, `+250 798 875 272`, `250-798-875-272`) are correctly rejected with HTTP 400 and 'You entered our collection account...' message. Root cause: the normalizer's if-condition `len(digits) == 9 and digits.startswith(('7', '0'))` never fires for `0798875272` because that string has 10 digits — the branch was written for 9-digit numbers only. This is a HIGH-priority safety fix — the merchant MSISDN is currently NOT protected from the local leading-zero format the review explicitly listed as a required blocked format. Direction audit (source grep) confirmed: `debit.payer_identifier=payer` (user input) and `credits[0].payee_identifier=BESOFT_PAYOUT_MSISDN` — never swapped. Guard is invoked in both endpoints. Frontend: checkout MoMo phone input renders blank `+250 ` (no auto-fill), hint text visible, merchant number → 'You entered our collection account...' banner, customer number → 'MTN MoMo temporarily unavailable...' + Stripe fallback banner. VOD screen MoMo phone input also renders blank `+250 `.

CRITICAL (safety): Fix `_normalize_msisdn` in /app/backend/server.py (lines 728-733) to convert 10-digit local numbers starting with '0' to E.164 (prefix '250', strip the leading '0'). Suggested code:
    digits = ''.join(ch for ch in phone if ch.isdigit())
    if len(digits) == 10 and digits.startswith('0'):
        digits = '250' + digits[1:]
    elif len(digits) == 9 and digits.startswith('7'):
        digits = '250' + digits
    return digits
After fix, re-run /app/backend/tests/test_momo_payer_guard.py — all 14 tests should pass.

rca_of_issue:
REPRODUCTION: POST /api/billing/momo/initiate with body {plan:'basic_monthly', phone:'0798875272'} (or same via VOD endpoint) returns HTTP 200 and reaches BeSoft, instead of the expected HTTP 400 'collection account' rejection. Verified via curl and pytest.

ROOT CAUSE: `_normalize_msisdn` at /app/backend/server.py:728-733 only recognises 9-digit local numbers:
    if len(digits) == 9 and digits.startswith(('7', '0')):
        digits = '250' + digits.lstrip('0')
The common Rwandan MTN format is 10 digits: `0798875272` (leading zero + 9 subscriber digits). This 10-digit string never satisfies `len(digits) == 9`, so it is returned unchanged. Result: guard compares '0798875272' vs '250798875272' → not equal → request forwarded to BeSoft. BeSoft then rejects with HTTP_400 (unrelated), so the user sees a generic error and never learns they accidentally targeted the merchant account.

MITIGATION (main agent to apply): update `_normalize_msisdn` to also handle 10-digit local format:
    if len(digits) == 10 and digits.startswith('0'):
        digits = '250' + digits[1:]
    elif len(digits) == 9 and digits.startswith('7'):
        digits = '250' + digits
After this, `_normalize_msisdn('0798875272')` → `250798875272` and the guard rejects the request with HTTP 400 as required.

IMPACT: safety-critical. Without the fix, a user could accidentally attempt to debit the merchant's own collection account using the natural leading-zero format they see on their phone. Even though BeSoft currently rejects downstream (HTTP_400 provider), if BeSoft ever accepted the request the merchant would be debited into their own account — a real financial risk.
